author: opt-W1b

contract.sync_assumed: none beyond convergence of the logical warp
contract.k_range: [1, N] with MaxK = round_up(k, LW) <= N, k 8 to 64 measured
contract.n_range: N = LW x IPT, measured 32 to 256 at LW 32
contract.type_constraints: cub::detail::WarpBitonicTopK as on the branch, keys-only on a (key, index) struct with the composite comparator (key first, smaller index first among equal keys) written branch-free with | and &, fp32 and bf16 keys, int32 indices
contract.nan_behavior: comparisons with NaN are false, a NaN lands at an unspecified position, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal under both requirements
contract.tie_break_support: exact prefer_smaller_index through the unchanged primitive at 1.03x to 1.24x (fp32) and 1.35x to 1.50x (bf16) the latency of the not_guaranteed reference and 0.54x to 0.72x its throughput (this card); the index-in-key route (W1_eager_same) gives the same result at 0.8x to 0.5x of this card's cycles
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted

correctness_notes: Oracle battery passed on every measured cell (exact prefer_smaller_index result, tie_heavy, all_equal, pivot_tie and signed_zero included). One cell of the first batch (bf16 N 256 k 8, random pattern) was dropped by the harness before its oracle ran: the cell binary exited with CUDA error 46 (device busy or unavailable) at the first allocation, a transient of the shared node, and the identical variant cell passed its oracle and measured 8319 cycles in the second batch one minute later. Controls in the same lock section: W1_baseline under prefer_smaller_index (first batch) and W1_reference under not_guaranteed (second batch, harness 0.3 --control-req). W1 was run by two optimizer instances after a duplicate launch: opt-W1 (worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1, variants W1_packed, W1_level, W1_reference_sub) and opt-W1b (this card, worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1b, variants W1_eager_same, W1_level_same, W1_minmax_pairs, W1_level_pairs, W1_baseline, W1_kvcmp and their _sub forms). opt-W1b owns the N2 kill experiment on identical network code, the fp32 native min max pairs route and the sub-warp grid.

low_level: fp32 N 128 k 32 latency kernel: 1840 SASS instructions against 3448 for the short-circuit comparator (W1_baseline) and 1152 for the not_guaranteed reference. BSSY, BSYNC and BRA (300, 300 and 305 in the short-circuit form) are gone, FSETP 612 to 462 (reference 306), PLOP3 449 to 189, FSEL 148 to 154, ISETP 455 to 409, 300 SHFL in all three. The struct key goes through the generic word path of warp_shuffle_xor, two shuffles per stage as the pairs reference.

bf16 N 128 k 32: 2280 against 2672 (reference 1656). Neither bf16 form has branches, the __hgt and __heq intrinsics are branch-free, and the gain is the predicate chain: PLOP3 455 to 189, P2R 58 to 23, HSETP2 462 in both (the composite comparator evaluates __hgt and __heq per call, the reference one __hgt).

Registers 23 to 74 (bf16 N 256 k 64: 74 against 52 for the short-circuit form and 42 for the reference), fp32 24 to 70 (reference 19 to 59), no spills, 6 blocks per SM from N 128 on against 8 for the reference, which with twice the instructions per exchange halves the throughput.
algorithmic: Against the short-circuit comparator (same primitive, same instantiation, prefer_smaller_index): fp32 3.5x at N 32 (721 against 2541), 5.4x at N 64 (1081 against 5876), 6.1x at N 128 k 32 (2120 against 12899), 5.5x at N 256 k 32 (4860 against 26895), 5.7x at N 256 k 64 (5902 against 33467); bf16 1.30x at N 32 (1072 against 1396), 1.28x to 1.40x at N 64, 1.44x to 1.48x at N 128 k <= 32, 2.49x at N 128 k 64 (2621 against 6526), 1.56x to 1.59x at N 256. Throughput fp32 1.7x to 1.9x (117 against 69 Gelem/s at N 32, 98 against 52 at N 256), bf16 1.16x to 1.24x.

The cost of prefer_smaller_index through the unchanged primitive with a branch-free struct comparator, against the not_guaranteed reference: fp32 1.24x at N 32 (721 against 583), 1.17x at N 64 (1081 against 925), 1.03x to 1.04x at N 128 k <= 32 (2120 against 2041 and 2062), 0.85x at N 128 k 64 (1821 against 2152), 1.06x at N 256 k <= 32 (4860 against 4606), 1.16x at N 256 k 64; bf16 1.38x at N 32, 1.35x to 1.37x at N 64, 1.45x to 1.50x at N 128 k <= 32, 1.02x at N 128 k 64, 1.40x to 1.48x at N 256 k <= 32, 2.10x at N 256 k 64 (9788 against 4658). Throughput 0.54x to 0.59x for fp32 (101 against 179 Gelem/s at N 128) and 0.67x to 0.72x for bf16.

Against the index-in-key route to the same result (W1_eager_same card, same session): the struct route is 1.17x to 1.27x slower for fp32 (721 against 601, 1081 against 934, 2120 against 1917, 4860 against 3826) with 0.55x to 0.63x the throughput, and 1.9x to 3.5x slower for bf16 (1072 against 574, 1598 against 761, 3400 against 1211, 8338 against 2371) with 0.28x to 0.35x the throughput. A comparator fix makes the struct route usable, the packing makes it unnecessary.
negative: The struct comparator route to prefer_smaller_index is never the best route: fixed, it costs 3 to 24 percent latency (fp32) and 35 to 50 percent (bf16) and 30 to 45 percent throughput against the not_guaranteed reference, where index-in-key costs nothing.
surprises: fp32 N 128 k 64 with the struct comparator (1821 cycles) is faster than the not_guaranteed pairs reference (2152) and the fastest fp32 N 128 cell after the min max pairs (1217): the two-register MaxK 64 tile gives a chain of one sort plus one merge, and the struct network's schedule happens to be good there (T28).
open_questions: Whether cub's WarpBitonicSortNetwork should document the comparator rule (T35) or whether a wrapper that forces the comparator result through a bool temporary before the select would make the short-circuit form harmless, not tried.
